title: Will Osborne, Benny Meroff, Ted Weems and Perry Como
summary: He recalls film work with Will Osborne and Meroff, radio singers who became famous, and Perry Como with Ted Weems.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You said you worked with Buddy Rogers. Did you ever know Will Osborne? Didn't he ever?
I worked with Will Osborne. Yeah, who was he? I made a picture of Blue's of the Night with Will Osborne. Oh, with that band, I see.
Yeah. Did you record with Buddy Rogers and Benny Murroff and Will Osborne?

No. No records, just movies. They never did make a record, those guys. That's funny. You know, that's a funny thing. Benny Murroff, I don't think, ever made a record, and he was very popular. Yeah. You see, we were at the Palace Theater in New York, with Eddie Cannon and Georgia Jessel. Now, that same part of the terrific show, they had Buddy Rogers with nobody and nobody knew them. Like Lucy, you know, Lucy, well, she used to work on radios, when I played radios, and nobody knew her, you know. And she, you think, Dina Show, when I was with Al Pierce, used to sing once every two, three weeks with Al Pierce. She didn't have a study job. And all these people get so big, but me. Yeah. You know, and I can't, and I, oh, you know when I worked with Ted Weems, Perry Como sang it
And there's another guy, I thought it was just another singer, see. Yeah. I said, gee. And I think that, Perry Como got so big too. Yeah. You know.
Well, Ted Weems had some good musicians.
Oh, Tandor, Al Motano, you know. Well, I like Country Washburn. Country Washburn. Yeah, he was a good musician.
